newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER-MONACO CONCENTRATE ON THE NEXT TASK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONACO CONCENTRATE ON THE NEXT TASK.

text.p: UEFA Cup semifinalists Monaco will allow themselves no rest as they turn their sights back on the French first division this weekend.
Their 3-0 demolition of Newcastle United in the second leg of their UEFA Cup quarter-final at home on Tuesday might seem a hard act to follow.
But coach Jean Tigana has coaxed such acts out of his talented team all season and aims to do the same for Saturday's home clash with third-placed Bastia.

"I'm satisfied, because we managed a faultless (performance) but from now I'm thinking about the Bastia match," Tigana said immediately after Tuesday night's match which saw Monaco reach the semifinals 4-0 on aggregate.
"We must get refocused and recover. There are three points to take and a title to lift."

Tigana is aided by the thirst for success of an aging squad who have been together for many seasons without winning a major trophy since the French Cup in 1991. Monaco's last of five league titles was in 1988.

Sylvain Legwinski, who scored Monaco's opening goal against Newcastle just before halftime, said: "(The victory) is the fruit of a collective pressing job... Now, I hope we'll get to the final. We have the means and the will."

Defensive midfielder Gilles Grimandi, like Legwinski a product of the Monaco youth teams developed by former coach Arsene Wenger, said: "Our strength this season has been in knowing how to shape our destiny, how to negotiate important turning points and redress the balance after bad ones."

Grimandi was referring to such moments as a 1-0 defeat by Borussia Monechengladbach in the home leg of their UEFA Cup second round tie after an impressive 4-2 away victory after which Tigana admitted they had relaxed their concentration.
Especially positive results include the 2-0 home win over championship rivals Paris St Germain in January and the 1-0 win in Newcastle following a 2-0 defeat at Metz.
In the league, their response to the Metz defeat was a 0-0 draw at home to current champions Auxerre followed by a 3-0 away victory at Rennes last week.

Legwinski, however, is one of two Monaco players booked on Tuesday night who will be suspended for the first leg of the semifinal. The other is captain and libero Franck Dumas, who has already served one suspension during the competition.
Legwinski's strike and two second half goals by midfielder Ali Benarbia show that Monaco are not reliant exclusively on their forwards to find the net.
Benarbia has now scored three times in the competition, only one less than Brazilian striker Anderson and two short of Nigeria's Victor Ikpeba.
Newcastle United manager Kenny Dalglish believes Monaco can go all the way and win their first European trophy after losing the 1993 Cup Winners' Cup final.
"They have pace up front and they're better away from home. They beat two German teams away and they beat us away," he said.
They have also not conceded a goal at home in nine matches dating back to early November.

Monaco's biggest success over Newcastle was in mastering the English virtues of combativity and speed and imposing their skill and technique as they became the first French side for 20 years and third in all to eliminate an English team from European competition.
Dalglish said his side could learn from Monaco as they sought to improve their game for future European competitions.
"(But) first we have to succeed at home," added Dalglish.
